focus: Iteration 2: packet 039 child 001, the question dialog after prepare: Stop states that cannot arm, other hold-open Claude dialogs, unreadable or malformed records, and the Pi, OpenCode and Codex question tools
noveltyJustification: 9 of 14 findings are fully new (Stop failure-state enumeration, the prompt-escape split, Claude hold-open event visibility, malformed-record shape, runtime question-tool inventory and per-runtime arm events); 5 confirm recorded limitations with the deciding lines.
keyQuestions: Packet 039 residual gaps: for each known limitation of children 001, 002 and 003 of packet 039 (a pending record Stop cannot arm, other dialogs that hold a turn open, an unreadable record, the same gap on Pi, OpenCode and Codex, a goal cleared by hand that comes back, a stale parent goal that is picked, a title ending in the hop number, the cost of one more log search), is it real in the code, how does it fail, and what is the smallest change?
ruledOut: Treating the deferred example as the worst stuck state; it is the one state a prompt already clears.
Widening the Claude prompt withdrawal to pending:any; it would withdraw a record prepared in the same turn.
A Claude PermissionRequest binding as today's smallest fix; the eventOrder cannot render it and the envelope shape is event-specific.
Reusing the ask-surface guard as the multi-runtime hop guard; it re-prompts prose menus and cannot block end-of-run events.

label: CONFIRMED limitation 5: pendingHandOver denies on any readable record whose armableRecord verdict is pending; armableRecord returns pending on status alone.

CONFIRMED: after a successful read, Stop leaves a pending record unchanged when transcript_path is missing, no killer target pid resolves, or arm throws or returns non-armed; these are the states the guard keeps refusing.

CONFIRMED: only the background-task deferral writes deferredAt, and the Claude UserPromptSubmit withdrawal accepts only a pending record with deferredAt; a prompt therefore clears a deferred record but not a missing-transcript, missing-target-pid or arm-failure record. Only cancel (pending:any) or a later successful Stop clears those.

Smallest fix for item 1: mark every post-read pending record that Stop cannot arm through markDeferred in armPendingRecord, so the existing prompt-withdraw policy clears it; do not widen the nudge to pending:any because that would withdraw a record prepared in the same turn.

CONFIRMED limitation 6 for plan approval: PreToolUse matches every built-in tool except EndConversation, ExitPlanMode is one of them and requires user interaction, but the registry matcher is AskUserQuestion only; an ExitPlanMode approval after prepare can park the hop.

CONFIRMED: a permission prompt is not PreToolUse-visible as a prompt; PreToolUse runs for every tool call while PermissionRequest runs only when Claude is about to ask, and exit code 2 is not honored on PermissionRequest. The Claude eventOrder has no PermissionRequest, so no such binding can render today; only Devin has one.

CONFIRMED: MCP elicitation is visible only through the Elicitation event (which can decline), Notification exposes permission_prompt and agent_needs_input but is observational and cannot end a turn, and EndConversation ends the conversation rather than holding it open; none is bound to the guard.

Smallest fix for item 2: accept ExitPlanMode in pendingHandOver and widen the registry matcher to AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode first; permission prompts need a new PermissionRequest eventOrder entry and an event-specific decision envelope, and elicitation a third binding.

CONFIRMED: an invalid-JSON record is logged as corrupt-relaunch-file and read as null; the guard fails open and allows the question while Stop returns without arming, so the prepared hop dies silently. The core read is tested but no guard or Stop test asserts the paired behavior.

CONFIRMED by reading: a parseable record with matching loopId, sessionId, runtime and status pending but no handoff is treated as pending; the guard denial interpolates undefined for the note path and armLocked can arm it without a handoff. No test feeds a shape-invalid record to the guard or Stop.

Smallest fix for item 3: validate required record fields in readRelaunchFile (non-empty handoff, loopId, sessionId, known status) and treat a shape failure like corrupt JSON; add a guard test with an invalid-JSON and a shape-invalid pending file, and a Stop test asserting no arm and the log line.

CONFIRMED: Pi, OpenCode and Codex each have a question tool (Pi ask_user_question or question, OpenCode question, Codex request_user_input) and none of the three relaunch adapters guards it while a hand-over is pending. Their arm events are agent_settled, session.idle and Stop, all of which a blocking question delays.

CONFIRMED: Codex, OpenCode and Pi withdraw only an armed record on a user message (pending:none), so answering the question does not clear a still-pending record; answering lets the run end and the arm event then fires, leaving an unanswered question at the context limit as the failure window.

Smallest fix per runtime for item 4: Codex reuses its existing PreToolUse event with a request_user_input matcher; OpenCode adds a tool.execute.before hook to the plugin; Pi adds a tool_call handler in the extension, whose event already carries a decision. Exact blocking semantics were not observed live this iteration.
Limitation 5 is real and broader than its example: the stuck states are the pending records Stop cannot arm, and only the deferred one has a prompt escape.
Limitation 6 is real for ExitPlanMode and permission prompts; the matcher and the Claude eventOrder are the two deciding bindings.
No guard or Stop test covers an unreadable or shape-invalid relaunch record; only the core read is tested.
The Pi, OpenCode and Codex adapters have the same question-tool exposure and no pending-hand-over guard.
A relaunch record is armed only after its required fields (handoff, loopId, sessionId, status) are validated.
Every parked pending hand-over has an operator escape other than the explicit cancel command.
